key_insight: Random data splits overestimate ML performance for perovskite photovoltaics because duplicate and near-duplicate devices leak across train/test sets; grouped splits expose the difference between memorization and true generalization.
engineering_relevance: A provenance-aware evaluation protocol helps researchers choose and trust models that better predict performance for new institutions, recipes, and future perovskite devices.
method: Mapped institutional provenance in the Perovskite Database
Built a hierarchy of grouped splits that isolate duplicates, publications, and institutions
Benchmarked 13 models across increasingly strict evaluation settings
evidence_signal: Nearly two-thirds of curated devices share an exact recipe with another, and model rankings change sharply when evaluation moves from random splits to unseen institutions and future discoveries.
watch_item: Results depend on the completeness and accuracy of provenance mapping, so missing or ambiguous metadata could weaken the grouped-split protocol.
paper_title: Provenance-grouped protocol for evaluating machine learning in perovskite photovoltaics
